findings.claim: Loop 4 regression in ci-no-secret-prints: a step that writes a secret to the run log now passes test 7. Reproduced on scratch copies under critic-work/education-recheck4 of the frozen export at HEAD 3c6a03a2 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 9278b451), npm ci in tests, Node v24.2.0, node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT; the critic wrote its own 26/26 solution (result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt) and ran one-change variants of it against the loop-4 grader and, for comparison, the loop-3 grader (tests/lab.mjs sha256 1cc3d198); no private overlay, staging, work folder, SME or reconciler folder was read. Shape: beside the README login, the login step adds a cat command opening an unquoted here-document whose body is the step-env variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD, with the cat output redirected to stderr and then piped into docker login with the username variable and --password-stdin. The loop-3 grader fails test 7 with the PRINTS_SECRET message; the loop-4 grader passes 26/26. Under bash 3.2.57 with set -eo pipefail, a stub docker and a dummy value, the value is written to stderr (the run log) and docker receives nothing on stdin. Cause: heredocs() now joins the rest of the opening line into the command (tests/lab.mjs line 642), so the exemption at line 666 sees a last stage of docker login --password-stdin and skips the body, and the command loop exempts the opening line as a login pipeline (lines 653-660), which checks only for a middle tee stage. The shape is outside the ops-sme-r2-03 heredoc list and the ops-sme-r1-02 pipeline list (which rules redirects in a login pipeline non-binding), and the echo-with-stderr-redirect analogue already passes on both graders, so no acceptance is unmet and no item reopens. It is untaught and off the README path, hence low.
findings.recommendation: Optional, tests/lab.mjs only: in the heredoc exemption (line 666), and in the login-pipeline exemption (lines 653-660), do not exempt a pipeline whose opening stage redirects its standard output (for example >&2, 1>&2 or >/dev/stderr), so the value that never reaches docker is judged as printed. If the reconciler keeps redirects non-binding as in ops-sme-r1-02, record this as accepted debt.
